name: issue_786_tou_precondition_banks_then_coasts
description: A cost_period schedule tagged 'high' from 16:15-21:00. Before the schedule's lead-time window opens, the home holds its normal comfort band (ceiling=comfort_cool=76F, cool mode). Once the window opens (fallback lead time 120min, since no thermal model observations exist -> opens 14:15), the automation engine banks toward the OPPOSITE comfort-band edge (comfort_heat=68F) instead -- no user-authored temperature field anywhere drove this, it is derived automatically from the existing comfort band. Once the schedule's own start time (16:15) is reached, pre-conditioning stops being called and the very next cycle's normal apply_classification() call re-arms the plain comfort_cool=76F ceiling on its own -- confirming the Issue #786 prerequisite finding that 'coast' behavior needs zero new suppression code, since _apply_comfort_band() issues a single-setpoint THRESHOLD command a real thermostat only acts on when indoor crosses it, not a proactive drive-to-target.
notes: (a) Scenario effectiveness: deleting coordinator._resolve_tou_schedule_state()/_apply_tou_schedule()'s call sites (or automation.py's apply_tou_precondition()) causes the 14:15 assertion (tou_precondition_applied, target=68.0) to FAIL -- no such event would ever fire, reproducing 'the TOU feature silently does nothing' exactly.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/scheduler-spec.md documents this exact resolve-then-act sequence and the coast-is-free finding; this scenario is the golden proof that production actually does what the spec says.

(c) Occupant experience: without this feature, the home runs the AC at its normal comfort_cool ceiling straight through a scheduled high-cost window (e.g. 4:15-9:00pm peak electricity rates), paying peak-rate cost with no cost-aware behavior. With it, the home banks extra coolness to comfort_heat before the window starts and coasts on that banked cool air through the expensive hours -- lower cost, and the occupant configured zero new temperature settings to get it; the system derived the banking target from settings they already had (comfort_heat) and the home's own learned response rate.

events.note: Hot afternoon. Indoor already at the normal comfort ceiling.
Before the TOU lead window opens (16:15 - 120min fallback lead = 14:15, since no thermal model observations exist yet). Normal comfort band arms: ceiling=comfort_cool=76F, cool mode.

Next 30-min cycle -- now sits exactly at the lead window's open instant (14:15). TOU pre-conditioning fires: banks to comfort_heat=68F (the OPPOSITE edge from the normal ceiling), cool mode, ahead of the 16:15 high-cost window. No temperature field was configured for this -- 68F is the home's own existing comfort_heat value.

Schedule's own start time reached -- TOU phase reverts to NONE (pre-conditioning stops being called this cycle). apply_classification()'s normal comfort-band arm (ceiling=comfort_cool=76F) is the only thing that runs -- confirming coast resumes with zero new suppression code, per the Issue #786 prerequisite finding.

assertions.reason: Normal 30-min classification cycle runs as always.
Before the TOU lead window opens, the plain comfort_cool ceiling (76F) is armed -- no TOU influence yet.

The lead window has opened -- production banks to comfort_heat=68F (cool mode) ahead of the 16:15 high-cost window, derived automatically from the existing comfort_heat config value and the home's own thermal response rate (fallback lead time here, since no observations exist).

Schedule start reached -- pre-conditioning stops firing, and the very next classification cycle's own normal comfort-band arm (ceiling=76F) is the final word. This is the coast confirmation: no separate suppression/coast-phase code exists anywhere in this feature -- the single-setpoint threshold command _apply_comfort_band() already issues is naturally idle while indoor sits below it, and simply resumes normal operation once pre-conditioning stops overriding it.

verdict.summary: TOU pre-conditioning banks to the comfort-band floor ahead of a scheduled high-cost window using zero user-authored temperature settings, then coasts back to normal comfort-band behavior automatically once the window starts, with zero new suppression code.
verdict.observed_behavior: Normal comfort_cool ceiling (76F) held before the lead window opens -> banks to comfort_heat (68F) once the fallback 120-minute lead window opens ahead of the 16:15 schedule -> reverts to the normal comfort_cool ceiling (76F) the instant the schedule's own start time is reached, with no dedicated coast-phase code involved.
verdict.expected_behavior: The occupant pays less to run AC during a scheduled expensive electricity window by having the home pre-cool using thermal mass it already has, using only settings (comfort_heat) and behavior (learned thermal rate) the system already knew about -- no new temperature configuration required for this feature to work.
